Rice Planting festival (around [[June 10]])
Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] * **Handa Shrine** ** deity: [[Konohana-no-Sakuya-Hime|Kono-hana-sakuya-hime]] * **Nakamiya Shrine** ** deity: [[Hoori|Fire-flashing deity]] * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Amenohoakari|Amenohoakari]] ** Located at the foot of Kanmuriyama in Godai Town. === Associated Shrines === * **Shisho Shrine** ** deity: [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi-no-mikoto]], [[Toyotama-Hime|Toyotama-hime]], accompanying the [[Tensonkorin]] * **Okutama Shrine** ** deity: [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-mikoto]] * **Kora Shrine** ** deity: [[Ame-no-uzume|Ame-no-uzume-no-mikoto]] * **Chuou Shrine** ** deity: Companion deity (Jurodaibu) == Main Events == * Archery festival (January 7) * Early Horse festival (Vernal Equinox) * Rice Planting festival (around June 10) - "Yakkorai" by residents of Kurano and Miyauchi areas (Intangible Cultural Property) * Mirror Cleansing festival (July 28) * Treasure Exposing festival (August 7) * festival (September 15) * Otsuya festival (Last Saturday of October) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (Nationally Designated) === * Flower and Bird Pattern Mirror - Inscribed with "Donated by Saemon-no-jo Tomotoshi on March 18, 1294" * Autumn Grass and Butterfly Mirror * Oak Tree and Hawk Hunting Mirror * Nitta Shrine Documents (9 volumes, 1 sheet) ** Nitta Shrine Records (1 volume), documents related to the Shuin family (7 volumes), documents related to the Ken Shuin family (1 volume), and a decree from Toyotomi Hideyoshi during the Kyushu Campaign (1 sheet) === Kagoshima Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Property === * Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] * **Handa Shrine** The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. It is believed to be the burial site of [[Ninigi no Mikoto]], the grandfather of [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2018-09-10 |title=Imperial tombs |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2018/09/11/imperial-tombs/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/2271/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=kic-update.com}} It has had a conflict with [[Hirasaki Shrine|Hirakiki jinja]] who also claimed to be the top shrine of the province{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社)　– Was Once The Highest ranking Shrine in Satsuma － {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/3133/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=kic-update.com}} There is a stone bridge called Korai-bashi (降来橋) in the shrine's [[Sandō]] ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Nitta Shrine | image = [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 1.jpg|270px|Nitta Shrine Chokushi Hall]]

Rice Planting festival (around [[June 10]])
Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. It is believed to be the burial site of [[Ninigi no Mikoto]], the grandfather of [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2018-09-10 |title=Imperial tombs |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2018/09/11/imperial-tombs/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/2271/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=kic-update.com}} It has had a conflict with [[Hirasaki Shrine|Hirakiki jinja]] who also claimed to be the top shrine of the province{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社)　– Was Once The Highest ranking Shrine in Satsuma － {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/3133/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=kic-update.com}} There is a stone bridge called Korai-bashi (降来橋) in the shrine's [[Sandō]] ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Nitta Shrine | image = [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 1.jpg|270px|Nitta Shrine Chokushi Hall]]

Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. It is believed to be the burial site of [[Ninigi no Mikoto]], the grandfather of [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2018-09-10 |title=Imperial tombs |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2018/09/11/imperial-tombs/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/2271/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=kic-update.com}} It has had a conflict with [[Hirasaki Shrine|Hirakiki jinja]] who also claimed to be the top shrine of the province{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社)　– Was Once The Highest ranking Shrine in Satsuma － {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/3133/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=kic-update.com}} There is a stone bridge called Korai-bashi (降来橋) in the shrine's [[Sandō]] ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Nitta Shrine | image = [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 1.jpg|270px|Nitta Shrine Chokushi Hall]]

Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." all the deities of [[Satsuma Province]] ([[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]) }} '''Nitta Shrine''' ({{lang-ja|新田神社 (薩摩川内市)}}) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Satsumasendai, Kagoshima|Satsumasendai]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], Japan. The Nitta Shrine houses two notable [[Setsumatsusha|subshrines]] the Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]] or a first ranked shrine of its province, and the Shukō Jinja, a [[Sōja shrine]] or a shrine that enshrines all the gods of its province. It contains Nitta Hachimangu, an [[ichinomiya]], and the first ranked shrine of [[Satsuma Province]] but itself is larger than merely that. It is located at the top of Mount Shinki (神亀山).,{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/travel/nitta-shrine-%E6%96%B0%E7%94%B0%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kic-update.com}} It is on a hill that overlooks the Sendai River.{{Cite web |title=Nitta Shrine |url=https://www.kagoshima-kankou.com/for/attractions/10417 |access-date=2023-05-08 |website=DISCOVER KAGOSHIMA / OFFICIAL TRAVEL GUIDE |language=en}} It enshrines [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]] an ancestor of the [[Imperial House of Japan]].{{Cite web |last=Sho |date=2015-10-04 |title=NITTA SHRINE – Praying Safe Birth of Child & Worship Japanese Emperor's Ancestor "NINIGI" {{!}} 地元人おすすめ！鹿児島観光ガイド！ |url=https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en,%20https://kagoshimalove.com/nitta-shrine/?lang=en/ |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=kagoshimalove.com |language=en}} In 1874, the Imperial Household Ministry identified the tomb located behind the shrine as the Mt. Kawai Mausoleum. It is believed to be the burial site of [[Ninigi no Mikoto]], the grandfather of [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2018-09-10 |title=Imperial tombs |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2018/09/11/imperial-tombs/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社) {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/2271/ |access-date=2023-05-16 |website=kic-update.com}} It has had a conflict with [[Hirasaki Shrine|Hirakiki jinja]] who also claimed to be the top shrine of the province{{Cite web |title=NITTA SHRINE (新田神社)　– Was Once The Highest ranking Shrine in Satsuma － {{!}} KAGOSHIMA Visitors' GUIDE {{!}} 鹿児島ビジターズガイド |url=http://kic-update.com/en/text-en/3133/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=kic-update.com}} There is a stone bridge called Korai-bashi (降来橋) in the shrine's [[Sandō]] ==Overview== {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Nitta Shrine | image = [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 1.jpg|270px|Nitta Shrine Chokushi Hall]]
Chokushi Hall | location = [[Kagoshima Prefecture]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]] 1935-2 | coordinates = {{Coord|31|49|39.5|N|130|17|33.6|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]
[[Amaterasu-omikami]]
[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]] | Shrine rank = [[Satsuma Province]] [[Ichinomiya]]
Former [[Kokuhusha]]
[[Beppyo Shrine]] | Foundation = Tradition: 2nd year of Shinki (725) | main hall = [[Irimoya-zukuri]] | Alternative names = | festival = [[September 15]] | Rituals = Archery festival ([[January 7]])
Rice Planting festival (around [[June 10]])
Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] * **Handa Shrine** ** deity: [[Konohana-no-Sakuya-Hime|Kono-hana-sakuya-hime]] * **Nakamiya Shrine** ** deity: [[Hoori|Fire-flashing deity]] * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Amenohoakari|Amenohoakari]] ** Located at the foot of Kanmuriyama in Godai Town. === Associated Shrines === * **Shisho Shrine** ** deity: [[Hoori|Hikohohodemi-no-mikoto]], [[Toyotama-Hime|Toyotama-hime]], [[Ugayafukiaezu|Ugayafukiaezu-no-mikoto]], [[Tamayori-Hime|Tamayori-hime]] * **Takeuchi Shrine** ** deity: [[Tate-no-uchi|Hiko-oshimachi-no-mikoto]] * **Twenty-Four Shrines** ** Deities: 24 deities accompanying the [[Tensonkorin]] * **Okutama Shrine** ** deity: [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-mikoto]] * **Kora Shrine** ** deity: [[Ame-no-uzume|Ame-no-uzume-no-mikoto]] * **Chuou Shrine** ** deity: [[Ooyamatsumi|Ooyamatsumi]] * **Hayakaze Shrine** ** deity: [[Shinatsuhiko|Shinatsuhiko]] * **Higashikadomori Shrine** ** deity: [[Toyoiwamado|Toyoiwamado-no-kami]] * **Nishikadomori Shrine** ** deity: [[Kushi-iwamado|Kushi-iwamado-no-kami]] * **Ukemochi Shrine** ** deity: [[Ukemochi]] * **Inari Shrine** ** deity: [[Ukanomitama|Ukanomitama-no-kami]] === Former Associated Shrines === * **Higan Shrine** ** deity: [[Fudoumyouou|Namikiri Fudo-myoo]] * **Ko Shrine** ** deity: [[Susanoo|Susanoo-no-mikoto]] === External Associated Shrines === * **Oonamuchi Shrine** ** deity: [[Oonamuchi]] * **Kurou Shrine** ** deity: [[Mikahaya|Mikahaya-no-kami]] * **Shuko Shrine** ** deity: [[Haya-hibi|Haya-hibi-no-kami]] * **Takeuchi Shrine** ** deity: [[Tate-no-uchi|Hiko-oshimachi-no-mikoto]] * **Daishogun Shrine** ** deity: [[Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]] * **Yatsuo Shrine** ** deity: [[Yamata-no-Orochi|Yamata-no-Orochi]], [[Yata-no-Kagami|Yata-no-Kagami]] * **Funamajima Shrine** ** deity: Companion deity (Jurodaibu) == Main Events == * Archery festival (January 7) * Early Horse festival (Vernal Equinox) * Rice Planting festival (around June 10) - "Yakkorai" by residents of Kurano and Miyauchi areas (Intangible Cultural Property) * Mirror Cleansing festival (July 28) * Treasure Exposing festival (August 7) * festival (September 15) * Otsuya festival (Last Saturday of October) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (Nationally Designated) === * Flower and Bird Pattern Mirror - Inscribed with "Donated by Saemon-no-jo Tomotoshi on March 18, 1294" * Autumn Grass and Butterfly Mirror * Oak Tree and Hawk Hunting Mirror * Nitta Shrine Documents (9 volumes, 1 sheet) ** Nitta Shrine Records (1 volume), documents related to the Shuin family (7 volumes), documents related to the Ken Shuin family (1 volume), and a decree from Toyotomi Hideyoshi during the Kyushu Campaign (1 sheet) === Kagoshima Prefecture Designated Tangible Cultural Property === * Shrine buildings (main hall, Worship Hall, Dance Hall, Chokushi Hall, side shrines) - main hall was built in the 3rd year of [[Kaei]] (1850) and resembles Buddhist architectural style{{Cite web|title=Nitta Shrine main hall, Worship Hall, Dance Hall, Chokushi Hall, Side Shrines|publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Education Committee|url=http://www.pref.kagoshima.jp/ba08/kyoiku-bunka/bunkazai/bunka/documents/5904_20120321152825-1.pdf|accessdate=2020-07-13|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203013516/http://www.pref.kagoshima.jp/ba08/kyoiku-bunka/bunkazai/bunka/documents/5904_20120321152825-1.pdf|archivedate=2013-12-03}}. Mirror Cleansing festival ([[July 28]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Kagoshima|label=Nitta Shrine|position=right|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) approach gate 1.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Entrance to the approach]] [[File:Nitta-shrine (satsuma-sendai) pavilions 2.jpg|200px|right|thumb|Chokushi Hall]] [[File:Nitta jinja Honden.JPG|200px|right|thumb|Dance Hall (left) and main hall (center back)]] '''Nitta Shrine''' (Nitta Jinja or Niita Jinja『Shinto Daijiten』 (Rinsen Shoten)) is a shrine located in [[Miyauchi Town (Satsumasendai)|Miyauchi Town]], [[Satsumasendai City]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Satsuma Province]]. The former [[shrine rank]] was [[Kokuhusha]], and it is currently a [[Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. Previously, as one of the Yawata Gosho Besshū, it enshrined the Yawata deity and was also known by various names such as '''"Nitta Hachimangu," "Hachiman Nitta Shrine," "Sendai Hachimangu," "Ichinomiya Hachiman,"''' and '''"Nitta Myojin."''' The burial mound behind the shrine was designated by the [[Imperial Household Agency]] in 1874 (Meiji 7) as the [[Imperial Mausoleum]] of [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto), known as the Kawaai Mausoleum. == Deities == * '''[[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]]''' * '''[[Amaterasu-omikami]]''' * '''[[Ame-no-oshihomimi|Masayakatsukatsu-hayahino-shinnohoseri-no-mikoto]]''' Until the [[Edo period]], the shrine enshrined [[Emperor Ojin]], [[Empress Jingu]], and [[Takenouchi no Sukune]] as the Yawata Trinity. == History == According to shrine tradition, [[[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] (Ninigi no Mikoto) arrived in the Sendai area from [[Kaseda]] in Kagoshima Prefecture and built a high palace called "Sennodaina-no-miya" in the area, giving rise to the name Sendai from "Sennodai." When Ninigi no Mikoto passed away, a tomb was constructed, which is now the Kawaai Mausoleum, and the shrine was founded to enshrine his spirit. The name "Nitta" reflects Ninigi no Mikoto's effort to create new rice fields in the area by diverting water from the Sendai River. The oldest record about Nitta Shrine is from the first year of [[Eiman]] (1165), which states that the shrine was rebuilt approximately 300 years earlier during the era of [[Emperor Seiwa]] (865 AD). Other records suggest the shrine was founded in the 2nd year of Shinki (725) during the reign of [[Emperor Shomu]] or in the 6th year of Gankyo (882) during the reign of [[Emperor Yozei]]. The shrine was previously known as Hachiman Nitta Shrine (Nitta Hachimangu), as it was one of the five Yawata Gosho Besshū established to pray for national peace during the [[Jōhei and Tengyō War]] (the rebellion of [[Taira no Masakado]] and [[Fujiwara no Sumitomo]]). This association is evidenced by historical documents from 1247 and 1357. Another tradition states that Nitta Shrine was originally located on the east side of Sendai River in the Miyazato area of [[Kumano Castle]] and later moved to its current location. This tradition is supported by the fact that the shrine site still retains the foundation stones of the original buildings. Despite not being mentioned in the [[Engishiki]], Nitta Shrine's importance is comparable to that of the [[Kashii Shrine]] in [[Fukuoka]], which also started as a mausoleum. In the [[Kamakura period]], [[Koremune Yasutoshi]], who shared ancestry with the [[Shimazu clan]], took the position of chief priest, and his descendants continued to serve as priests for generations. During the [[Mongol Invasions of Japan]], the [[Kamakura shogunate]] ordered prayers for protection at various shrines, including Nitta Shrine. [[Shimazu Tadahisa]] presented offerings to Nitta Shrine, recognizing it as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma, despite disputes with [[Hirakiki Shrine]]. Under the [[Modern shrine ranking system]], Nitta Shrine was initially unranked but was promoted to [[Kokuhusha]] in Meiji 18 (1885), surpassing Hirakiki Shrine. Currently, both shrines are classified as [[Beppyo Shrines]]. == Mausoleum == On July 10, 1874, the Meiji Emperor designated the Kawaai Mausoleum as the official tomb of [[Ninigi|Ninigi no Mikoto]]. The mausoleum, covering four-fifths of the shrine grounds, is managed by the Imperial Household Agency. The shrine-mausoleum integration is unique in Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == === Mausoleum Shrines === * **Kawaai Shrine** ** deity: [[Ninigi|[[Ninigi|Ame-no-hikahiko-hononinigi-no-mikoto]]]] *
